and.name: Model_Federation
and.description: Represents the NAOMI approach for enabling multiple models, developed using different DSMLs, to work together through a structured mechanism for linking and execution, addressing heterogeneity and modularity. Trace: [Article_1 §1 Introduction; Article_1 §4.2 Repository; Article_8 §chunk::4; Article_8 §chunk::15]

and.name: Structural
and.description: Covers the artefacts, links, and structural features of Model Federation, including model composition, graph structure, formalism, domain, technological context, and modeling spaces. Trace: [Article_1 §4.2 Repository; Article_1 §Connectors; Article_8 §chunk::42]

and.name: Infrastructure_Components
and.description: Abstract grouping for the software components that constitute the federation infrastructure, including the core concept space, technological connectors, and solvers. Trace: [Article_1 §4.2 Repository; Article_1 §Connectors; Article_13 §chunk::33; Article_8 §chunk::42; Article_9 §chunk::93]

and.name: Repository
and.description: The managed storage location where models and their corresponding editing tools reside inside the repository in their native forms. Trace: [Article_1 §4.2 Repository]

and.name: Connectors
and.description: Software components that connect individual models to the multi-model and allow controlled information exchange between models, including technological connectors for dynamic linking. Trace: [Article_1 §Connectors; Article_8 §chunk::42]

and.name: Lightweight_Design
and.description: A primary design goal of NAOMI to have simple, lightweight connectors enabling easy integration of new modeling languages and tools. Trace: [Article_1 §Connectors]

and.name: Language_Tool_Specificity
and.description: Connectors are language and tool specific, though they may be used for multiple tools if equivalent interfaces are provided. Trace: [Article_1 §Connectors]

and.name: Technological_Connectors
and.description: Connectors that establish dynamic links between the virtual model and the technological models. Trace: [Article_8 §chunk::42]

and.name: Openflexo
and.description: A model federation infrastructure chosen for its flexibility and maturity to support the methodology, evolving into a generic collaborative platform for multifaceted modeling and artifact generation, providing support for model federation across multiple technological spaces. Trace: [Article_11 §chunk::47; Article_13 §chunk::58; Article_8 §chunk::29]

and.name: Concept_Space
and.description: The actual core of the model federation engine that provides the designer with the necessary concepts for modeling. Trace: [Article_13 §chunk::33]

and.name: MMINT
and.description: A model management tool providing a graphical and interactive environment for model management. Trace: [Article_14 §chunk::4]

and.name: Vitruvius
and.description: An approach that formalizes the essential concept of virtual single underlying models and their properties to support consistency preservation and integration of existing models. Trace: [Article_2 §chunk::19]

and.name: OSM
and.description: Orthogonal Software Modeling approach that defines a development process with roles and organizes Single Underlying Models in dimensions to facilitate navigation. Trace: [Article_2 §chunk::39]

and.name: Specialized_Integration_Technologies
and.description: Technologies such as model transformation tools, tracing tools, or libraries for exposing services that realize specific aspects of a tool chain. Trace: [Article_3 §chunk::58]

and.name: Solver
and.description: An existing tool or component used to solve analysis models for different configurations and produce analysis results. Trace: [Article_9 §chunk::93]

and.name: Modelverse
and.description: A prototype tool implementation combining language engineering, model operations, and process modeling with support for enactment in a single tool. Trace: [Article_4 §chunk::8]

and.name: Tool_Structure
and.description: The structure of tools used in the development process, which can limit selection if not flexible. Trace: [Article_5 §chunk::221]

and.name: Federated_IDE
and.description: A federated tool-chain architecture (F-IDE) that manages the overall information model while supporting distributed architectures and centralized understanding. Trace: [Article_6 §chunk::13]

and.name: Standard_Engineering_Tools
and.description: Abstract grouping for standard engineering tools used in industrial organizations, such as Jira and CAD tools. Trace: [Article_6 §chunk::13]

and.name: Jira
and.description: A standard engineering tool used for issue tracking and project management in the development environment. Trace: [Article_6 §chunk::13]

and.name: CAD_Drawing_Tools
and.description: Standard engineering tools used for creating technical drawings and designs in the development environment. Trace: [Article_6 §chunk::13]

and.name: Proprietary_Tools
and.description: Abstract grouping for proprietary tools specific to an organization, such as those used for vehicle architecture and diagnostics. Trace: [Article_6 §chunk::15]

and.name: Specifier
and.description: A proprietary tool that centrally defines the communication network of all vehicle architectures. Trace: [Article_6 §chunk::15]

and.name: ModArc
and.description: A proprietary database that defines all hardware entities and their interfaces. Trace: [Article_6 §chunk::15]

and.name: Diagnostics_Tool
and.description: A proprietary tool that specifies the diagnostics functionality of all vehicle architectures. Trace: [Article_6 §chunk::15]

and.name: Requirements_Specifier
and.description: A proprietary tool that allows for the semi-formal specification of system requirements. Trace: [Article_6 §chunk::15]

and.name: Systems_Engineering_Tools
and.description: Abstract grouping for toolsuites used in systems engineering that focus on functional requirements and VV&A. Trace: [Article_7 §chunk::21]

and.name: CORE
and.description: A toolsuite that models a system domain focusing on functional requirements and VV&A. Trace: [Article_7 §chunk::21]

and.name: GENESYS
and.description: A toolsuite that models a system domain focusing on functional requirements and VV&A. Trace: [Article_7 §chunk::21]

and.name: Model_Representation
and.description: Abstract grouping for the different types of artifacts, their storage formats, and standards within the federation, including modeling spaces, heterogeneity, and analysis models. Trace: [Article_1 §4.2 Repository; Article_1 §Introduction; Article_13 §chunk::15; Article_8 §chunk::15; Article_9 §chunk::93]

and.name: DSML_Models
and.description: Models developed using different Domain Specific Modeling Languages (DSMLs) or specific tools like Matlab and BPMN that work together within the federation. Trace: [Article_1 §Introduction; Article_1 §4.4 Automated Multi-model Execution Engine; Article_13 §chunk::25; Article_8 §chunk::29]

and.name: UMLsec
and.description: An approach on top of UML used to study the evolution of system artifacts from conceptual to program level. Trace: [Article_11 §chunk::47]

and.name: SecBPMN
and.description: An extension of BPMN that contributes security annotations related to properties such as confidentiality or accountability. Trace: [Article_11 §chunk::14]

and.name: Matlab
and.description: A specific tool and algorithm environment used for analysis and design activities within the federation. Trace: [Article_13 §chunk::25]

and.name: WML
and.description: A language used in the emulation of component execution to generate executable operations in the target platform. Trace: [Article_7 §chunk::72]

and.name: BPMN
and.description: A business process modeling language used as an example of a specialized formalism. Trace: [Article_8 §chunk::29]

and.name: Analysis_Models
and.description: Models used to analyze non-functional properties and performance characteristics, often solved by existing solvers for different configurations. Trace: [Article_9 §chunk::43; Article_9 §chunk::93]

and.name: Native_Forms
and.description: The state in which models reside inside the repository, preserving their original format, including formats like Excel files. Trace: [Article_1 §4.2 Repository; Article_8 §chunk::29]

and.name: Excel_Files
and.description: Spreadsheet files used as a native form for storing data that can be synchronized with process models. Trace: [Article_8 §chunk::29]

and.name: Interfaces
and.description: The connection points provided by models or tools that connectors utilize to enable integration. Trace: [Article_1 §4.2 Repository; Article_1 §Connectors]

and.name: ROS_Protocol_Files
and.description: Interface files modeled using the Robot Operating System protocol, containing expected attribute types and names. Trace: [Article_5 §chunk::127]

and.name: Security_Annotations
and.description: Graphical syntax elements linked to existing model elements to define security properties and attributes. Trace: [Article_11 §chunk::14]

and.name: Knowledge_Base
and.description: Abstract grouping for the formal knowledge foundations and reference architectures used to support meaningful interoperation. Trace: [Article_10 §chunk::28; Article_10 §chunk::21]

and.name: Ontology
and.description: Formal techniques used to construct a formal knowledge foundation for simulation models and domain conceptual architecture. Trace: [Article_10 §chunk::28; Article_10 §chunk::21]

and.name: Reference_Model
and.description: A model built based on domain knowledge to formulate the domain conceptual architecture for meaningful interoperation. Trace: [Article_10 §chunk::28]

and.name: Common_Representation_Language
and.description: A language like RAS++ derived from MDE literature similarities, used in the core of a knowledge base for MDE. Trace: [Article_14 §chunk::4]

and.name: Consistency_Preservation_Language
and.description: Languages used within the Vitruvius process to define and enforce consistency preservation rules between models. Trace: [Article_2 §chunk::19]

and.name: Model_Integrated_Computing
and.description: A division of MDE that provides DSMLs and environments to generate executable application systems and support interoperation between subsystems. Trace: [Article_10 §chunk::33]

and.name: Multimodel
and.description: An integrated model structure used to combine different models representing various aspects of a system, specifically for integrating quality assessment in Model-Driven Engineering. Trace: [Article_12 §chunk::0; Article_12 §chunk::22]

and.name: Viewpoints
and.description: The constituent elements of the multimodel defined by the goals and questions of the GQM approach to represent specific system aspects. Trace: [Article_12 §chunk::16]

and.name: MDE_Standards
and.description: General purpose modeling standards such as OMG, MOF, UML, and Model Driven Architecture used for modeling environments, including UML profiles and MOF conformity mechanisms. Trace: [Article_13 §chunk::15; Article_8 §chunk::50]

and.name: OASIS_OSLC
and.description: An emerging interoperability open standard based on W3C Linked Data and REST, providing tool- and platform-neutral usage of web technologies. Trace: [Article_6 §chunk::11]

and.name: UML_Profiles
and.description: A mechanism for extending UML, though it poses problems with MOF conformity and extensibility in certain contexts. Trace: [Article_8 §chunk::50]

and.name: MOF_Conformity
and.description: A standard for metamodel conformity that can pose problems when extending metamodels using certain approaches. Trace: [Article_8 §chunk::50]

and.name: Megamodel
and.description: A model representing models and their relationships, used as a technique for architecture recovery and understanding MDE projects, and containing information for automated tasks. Trace: [Article_14 §chunk::4; Article_9 §chunk::93]

and.name: Metamodels
and.description: Artifacts defining the abstract syntax and structure of models, explicitly listed as a core artifact type in MDE projects, including extension mechanisms like EMF facets. Trace: [Article_14 §chunk::3; Article_8 §chunk::50]

and.name: EMF_Facets
and.description: A non-intrusive extension mechanism to add attributes, references, or operations on a model without modifying its metamodel. Trace: [Article_8 §chunk::50]

and.name: KerMeta
and.description: A metamodeling approach that deals with model heterogeneity by extending existing metamodels. Trace: [Article_8 §chunk::50]

and.name: Model_Transformations
and.description: Artifacts that convert models from one form to another, such as model-to-model or model-to-text transformations. Trace: [Article_14 §chunk::3]

and.name: M2T_Transformation
and.description: Model-to-text transformations executed to generate textual format files or code depending on the target platform. Trace: [Article_14 §chunk::6]

and.name: Virtual_Single_Underlying_Model
and.description: The essential concept in the Vitruvius approach representing a unified model that underlies various views and ensures consistency. Trace: [Article_2 §chunk::19]

and.name: Viewtypes
and.description: Definitions predefined by the methodologist that allow developers to derive specific views of the Virtual Single Underlying Model. Trace: [Article_2 §chunk::102; Article_2 §chunk::39]

and.name: GPPL
and.description: General Purpose Programming Language implementation used as an evaluation baseline for transformation rules, such as Java. Trace: [Article_2 §chunk::242]

and.name: Java
and.description: A specific General Purpose Programming Language used for PCM to Java rules and implementation in the Vitruvius case study. Trace: [Article_2 §chunk::242]

and.name: System_Architecture_Modeling
and.description: Abstract grouping for approaches that model system configuration, components, and the interrelations between function and form. Trace: [Article_3 §chunk::162]

and.name: Contact_and_Channel_Approach
and.description: A system architecture model approach that graphically represents a system configuration with underlying interrelations between function and form. Trace: [Article_3 §chunk::162]

and.name: Function_Modeling
and.description: Modeling performed utilizing a function database where interrelations between function and form are explicitly captured. Trace: [Article_3 §chunk::162]

and.name: Part_Library
and.description: A library utilized to create possible configurations of components and to further concretize functional constraints. Trace: [Article_3 §chunk::162]

and.name: Support_Model
and.description: Models that provide assistance in the architecting of viewpoints, specifically in the elaboration of viewpoint relations. Trace: [Article_3 §chunk::119]

and.name: Business_Process_Model
and.description: A general purpose or domain-specific language used as an example to describe tool chains by borrowing descriptions from other domains. Trace: [Article_3 §chunk::57]

and.name: FTG_PM
and.description: A formalism consisting of the Formalism Transformation Graph and the Process Model to provide an overview of formalisms, relations, and the development process. Trace: [Article_4 §chunk::15; Article_4 §chunk::16]

and.name: Formalism_Transformation_Graph
and.description: Presents all used formalisms as nodes and their relations as links, providing an overview of languages and operations used in the process. Trace: [Article_4 §chunk::16]

and.name: Process_Model
and.description: Mandates the order of operations to execute and specifies on which models (data) they operate within the FTG+PM approach. Trace: [Article_4 §chunk::16]

and.name: Implementation_Artifacts
and.description: Abstract grouping for various artifacts such as models, prototypes, and source code used for the realization of design decisions. Trace: [Article_5 §chunk::7]

and.name: Prototypes
and.description: Implementation artifacts used in the realization of design decisions during engineering. Trace: [Article_5 §chunk::7]

and.name: Source_Code
and.description: Implementation artifacts representing the code realization of the system. Trace: [Article_5 §chunk::7]

and.name: Off_the_Shelf_Components
and.description: Pre-existing components selected during the development process. Trace: [Article_5 §chunk::7]

and.name: Heterogeneous_Models
and.description: Distinct models representing different sections of the system, as opposed to heterogeneous views of a single model. Trace: [Article_5 §chunk::226]

and.name: Heterogeneous_Views
and.description: Different views of a model used to observe system consistency and define actions for inconsistencies. Trace: [Article_5 §chunk::226]

and.name: UML_Diagrams
and.description: Diagrams used to model the product from a hardware perspective, including connections and actions. Trace: [Article_5 §chunk::127]

and.name: GitHub
and.description: A tool used by software engineers to collaboratively develop software code and maintain communication interfaces. Trace: [Article_5 §chunk::127]

and.name: Visio
and.description: A tool used by mechatronics engineers to create UML diagrams for modeling the hardware perspective of a product. Trace: [Article_5 §chunk::127]

and.name: Network_of_Components
and.description: Abstract grouping for the functional, behavioral, and structural components of the system represented as a network. Trace: [Article_5 §chunk::217]

and.name: Functional_Components
and.description: Components within the network that represent the functional aspects of the system. Trace: [Article_5 §chunk::217]

and.name: Behavioral_Components
and.description: Components within the network that represent the behavioral aspects of the system. Trace: [Article_5 §chunk::217]

and.name: Structural_Components
and.description: Components within the network that represent the structural aspects of the system. Trace: [Article_5 §chunk::217]

and.name: Project_Structure
and.description: Abstract grouping for the development team organization, product structure, and change history. Trace: [Article_5 §chunk::217]

and.name: Development_Team_Organization
and.description: A structural aspect encompassing the organization of the development team within the project context. Trace: [Article_5 §chunk::217]

and.name: Product_Structure
and.description: A structural aspect representing the organization and composition of the product being developed. Trace: [Article_5 §chunk::217]

and.name: Change_History
and.description: A record of the changes and evolution of the system over time. Trace: [Article_5 §chunk::217]

and.name: Federated_IDE_Views
and.description: An integrated set of modelling views that cover the early phases of tool-chain development within the federated IDE. Trace: [Article_6 §chunk::2]

and.name: Resource_Allocation_View
and.description: A view in the model where the architect can obtain an overview of the coupling/cohesion of the tools and identify producer/consumer relations. Trace: [Article_6 §chunk::50]

and.name: Domain_Specification_View
and.description: A view where the architect views the dependencies between the different domains irrespective of resource deployment. Trace: [Article_6 §chunk::50]

and.name: Resource_Shapes
and.description: A concept used in linked data modelling to define the structure of resources. Trace: [Article_6 §chunk::2]

and.name: Information_Model
and.description: The overall information model handled within the federated environment, managed through explicitly defined meta-models. Trace: [Article_6 §chunk::3; Article_6 §chunk::13]

and.name: Functional_Flow_Representation
and.description: Abstract grouping for methods used to document process flow and visualize the time sequence of events. Trace: [Article_7 §chunk::72]

and.name: FFBD
and.description: A structured method for documenting process flow, visualizing the time sequence of events and order of execution of system functions. Trace: [Article_7 §chunk::72; Article_7 §chunk::21]

and.name: Modeling_Spaces
and.description: Abstract grouping for the different spaces involved in model federation, such as conceptual and technological spaces. Trace: [Article_8 §chunk::42]

and.name: Conceptual_Space
and.description: The space containing the virtual model and projected concepts, mapped to the technological space. Trace: [Article_8 §chunk::42]

and.name: Technological_Space
and.description: The space containing the actual technological models and DSLs used in development. Trace: [Article_8 §chunk::42]

and.name: Virtual_Model
and.description: A model representing the conceptual space that is dynamically linked to technological models via connectors and slots. Trace: [Article_8 §chunk::42]

and.name: Modeling_Space_Heterogeneity
and.description: The heterogeneity introduced by the use of specialized formalisms, tools, and DSLs in the modeling space. Trace: [Article_8 §chunk::15]

and.name: Structural_Links
and.description: Abstract grouping for the relationships and graph structures defined between federated models, including semantic links and model slots. Trace: [Article_1 §4.2 Repository; Article_1 §4.4 Automated Multi-model Execution Engine; Article_13 §chunk::25; Article_8 §chunk::42]

and.name: Model_Dependency_Graph
and.description: A graph built based on each model's inputs and outputs to represent relationships within the project. Trace: [Article_1 §4.2 Repository; Article_1 §4.4 Automated Multi-model Execution Engine]

and.name: Macromodels
and.description: Models used to capture how models are related to each other and to analyze if those relationships are satisfied, often utilized for model management and architectural design. Trace: [Article_12 §chunk::8]

and.name: Semantic_Links
and.description: Links capturing the mapping between architecture model elements and process activities to support orchestration and maturity improvement. Trace: [Article_13 §chunk::25]

and.name: Model_Slots
and.description: Mechanisms used to establish dynamic links between the virtual model and technological models. Trace: [Article_8 §chunk::42; Article_8 §chunk::29]

and.name: Conformance_Relationship
and.description: A relationship indicating that a model conforms to a metamodel, defining its validity. Trace: [Article_14 §chunk::6]

and.name: Transformation_Application_Relationship
and.description: A relationship linking a transformation to its input and output models. Trace: [Article_14 §chunk::6]

and.name: Invocation_Relationship
and.description: A relationship indicating that one artifact calls or invokes another, such as a Java file calling an Acceleo module. Trace: [Article_14 §chunk::6]

and.name: Requirements_Tracing
and.description: A network that traces the connection between requirements, function, component structure, and the detailed design process. Trace: [Article_5 §chunk::217]

and.name: Resource_Dependencies
and.description: Dependencies between resources that are described as part of the system structure. Trace: [Article_5 §chunk::221]

and.name: Producer_Consumer_Relations
and.description: Direct dependencies between tools that can be identified in the Resource Allocation View. Trace: [Article_6 §chunk::50]

and.name: Indirect_Dependencies
and.description: Dependencies between tools that are not direct producer/consumer relations, identifiable in the Resource Allocation View. Trace: [Article_6 §chunk::50]

and.name: Interoperability_Levels
and.description: Abstract grouping for the different levels of interoperability defined by the software implementation details and data interpretation, including conceptual interoperability. Trace: [Article_10 §chunk::13; Article_13 §chunk::58]

and.name: Syntactic_Interoperability
and.description: A level of interoperability dealing with the software implementation details of interoperation and data exchange. Trace: [Article_10 §chunk::13]

and.name: Semantic_Interoperability
and.description: A level of interoperability involving exchange of data elements based on a common data interpretation. Trace: [Article_10 §chunk::13]

and.name: Conceptual_Interoperability
and.description: Interoperability achieved through models federation, extending beyond syntactic and semantic levels to support conceptual alignment. Trace: [Article_13 §chunk::58]

and.name: Common_Syntactic_Representation
and.description: An approach to model integration that transforms various models into a common language or meta-model to provide a unified syntactic structure. Trace: [Article_7 §chunk::29]

and.name: Linked_Data_Approach
and.description: An approach promoted by the architecture of the Internet to achieve massive scalability and flexibility in distributed systems. Trace: [Article_6 §chunk::11; Article_6 §chunk::13]

and.name: REST_Architectural_Pattern
and.description: The Representational State Transfer pattern followed by OASIS OSLC to achieve high cohesion between tools. Trace: [Article_6 §chunk::11]

and.name: Operational
and.description: Includes the processes, operations, and triggers in Model Federation, focusing on querying, synchronisation, validation, and management of federated models and links, including translation and composition approaches. and.name: Execution_Process
and.description: Abstract grouping for the mechanisms and engines that drive the execution of federated models, including orchestration. Trace: [Article_1 §4.4 Automated Multi-model Execution Engine; Article_13 §chunk::25]

and.name: Automated_Multi_Model_Execution_Engine
and.description: The engine that facilitates the generation of a workflow for integrated DSMLs in the context of a NAOMI project. Trace: [Article_1 §4.4 Automated Multi-model Execution Engine]

and.name: Workflow_Generation
and.description: The process facilitated by AMMEE to create a workflow for integrated DSMLs. Trace: [Article_1 §4.4 Automated Multi-model Execution Engine]

and.name: Dependency_Resolution
and.description: The action performed when execution of a project is requested to resolve dependencies between models. Trace: [Article_1 §4.4 Automated Multi-model Execution Engine]

and.name: Model_Registry_Query
and.description: The operation where AMMEE queries the model registry for all registered models during execution planning. Trace: [Article_1 §4.4 Automated Multi-model Execution Engine]

and.name: Execution_Plan
and.description: The plan of execution generated by AMMEE based on the dependency graph. Trace: [Article_1 §4.2 Repository; Article_1 §4.4 Automated Multi-model Execution Engine]

and.name: Orchestration
and.description: The process of mapping architecture elements to process activities to support continuous maturity improvement. Trace: [Article_13 §chunk::25]

and.name: Enactment
and.description: The execution of the series of operations defined in the process model, starting at the initial node and creating or modifying linked models. Trace: [Article_4 §chunk::4; Article_4 §chunk::16]

and.name: Integration_Process
and.description: Abstract grouping for the operational aspects of integrating and maintaining consistency between models, including artifact generation, feedback of analysis results, and approaches like translation or composition. Trace: [Article_1 §Connectors; Article_1 §1 Introduction; Article_13 §chunk::58; Article_8 §chunk::8; Article_9 §chunk::4]

and.name: Controlled_Information_Exchange
and.description: The capability provided by connectors to allow information exchange between models in a controlled manner. Trace: [Article_1 §Connectors]

and.name: Data_Exchange
and.description: The process of exchanging data elements based on a common data interpretation to achieve interoperability. Trace: [Article_10 §chunk::13]

and.name: Change_Propagation
and.description: The coordination of necessary model changes to other dependent models. Trace: [Article_1 §1 Introduction]

and.name: Tool_Integration
and.description: The capability to integrate new modeling languages and tools into the NAOMI infrastructure. Trace: [Article_1 §Introduction; Article_1 §Connectors]

and.name: Multimodel_Definition_Process
and.description: The operational process of defining a multimodel by considering different formalisms and selecting the one that best fits organizational and technological needs for each concern. Trace: [Article_12 §chunk::22]

and.name: Artifact_Generation
and.description: The capability of the modeling infrastructure to generate artifacts such as documents and code. Trace: [Article_13 §chunk::58]

and.name: Integration_of_Existing_Models
and.description: Approaches to enable developers to use Vitruvius with models created without it, which may lack required correspondences or adherence to consistency rules. Trace: [Article_2 §chunk::187]

and.name: Co_simulation_and_Optimization
and.description: An area of tool integration covering co-simulation and optimization activities. Trace: [Article_3 §chunk::148]

and.name: Model_Operations
and.description: Operations that specify possible mappings between languages in the context of Multi-Paradigm Modelling. Trace: [Article_4 §chunk::8]

and.name: Data_Allocation
and.description: The allocation of data within the system, described as part of the system structure. Trace: [Article_5 §chunk::221]

and.name: Translation_Approach
and.description: An approach oriented towards model transformations to bring all DSLs under one operating paradigm. Trace: [Article_8 §chunk::8]

and.name: Unification_through_Intermediate_Languages
and.description: An approach that aims to unify heterogeneous concerns through the use of intermediate languages. Trace: [Article_8 §chunk::8]

and.name: Composition_of_Metamodels
and.description: An approach to integration that involves the composition of metamodels. Trace: [Article_8 §chunk::8]

and.name: Feedback_of_Analysis_Results
and.description: The mechanism for returning analysis results from analysis models back to the software models or process to support design decisions. Trace: [Article_9 §chunk::4]

and.name: Software_Process_Automation
and.description: Abstract grouping for the automation of software process tasks to minimize human interventions and improve efficiency by leveraging the megamodel. Trace: [Article_9 §chunk::108; Article_9 §chunk::4]

and.name: Minimize_Human_Intervention
and.description: The objective of reducing the need for human input by retrieving information automatically from the ecosystem of modeling artifacts. Trace: [Article_9 §chunk::108]

and.name: Automated_Query_Retrieval
and.description: The capability to retrieve hidden information from artifacts or the megamodel by asking the right query during process execution. Trace: [Article_9 §chunk::108]

and.name: Development_Process
and.description: Abstract grouping for the roles and activities involved in the development process of a system using a Virtual Single Underlying Model. Trace: [Article_2 §chunk::19; Article_2 §chunk::39]

and.name: Methodologist
and.description: A role responsible for selecting metamodels, defining consistency preservation, and defining viewtypes at the metamodel level. Trace: [Article_2 §chunk::102; Article_2 §chunk::39]

and.name: Developer
and.description: A role that uses viewtypes to create, access, and manipulate the V-SUM and derive views for the system under consideration. Trace: [Article_2 §chunk::102; Article_2 §chunk::39]

and.name: Architecting_Viewpoints
and.description: The process of selecting viewpoints and elaborating their relations, supported by support models, emphasizing product concepts and overall architecture. Trace: [Article_3 §chunk::119]

and.name: VDI2206_Process
and.description: A standard process covering the design from initial conceptualization to verification and validation phases, though it does not explicitly address relations between viewpoints. Trace: [Article_3 §chunk::163]

and.name: Language_Engineering
and.description: The aspect of Multi-Paradigm Modelling that specifies the nodes (formalisms) in the Formalism Transformation Graph. Trace: [Article_4 §chunk::8]

and.name: Evolution_Process
and.description: Processes focused on managing the evolution of system artifacts and models to prevent inconsistency, supporting agile methodologies, concurrent development, and incremental propagation of changes. Trace: [Article_11 §chunk::47; Article_11 §chunk::3; Article_13 §chunk::2; Article_9 §chunk::43]

and.name: Inter-artifact_Tracing
and.description: A technique used to study the evolution of system artifacts by tracing relationships between them. Trace: [Article_11 §chunk::47]

and.name: Trace_Based_Identification
and.description: A method to identify relationships between artifacts based on the type of referring artifact and details of the reference. Trace: [Article_14 §chunk::5]

and.name: Graph_Transformation_Techniques
and.description: Techniques employed to synchronize models during the evolution process. Trace: [Article_11 §chunk::47]

and.name: Synchronization
and.description: The process of aligning models to ensure consistency as they evolve. Trace: [Article_11 §chunk::47]

and.name: Agile_Methodologies

and.name: Co_evolution

and.name: Reconciliation

and.name: Concurrent_Development

and.name: Refinement

and.name: Alteration

and.name: Updates

and.name: Consistency_Across_Tools

and.name: Evaluation_Method

and.name: Execution_Time_Measurement

and.name: Coupling_Cohesion_Analysis

and.name: Change_Impact_Analysis

and.name: Software_Evolution_Analysis

and.name: NFP_Analysis

and.name: Design_Space_Search

and.name: Metaheuristics

and.name: Intentional

and.name: Modeling_Paradigm_Support

and.name: Multi_Formalism_Approach

and.name: Diverse_Modeling_Paradigms
and.description: The ability to combine different modeling paradigms, serving as a testbed for exploration. Trace: [Article_1 §1 Introduction]

and.name: Concern_Based_Modeling

and.name: Model_Centric_Approach
and.description: An approach where the modeling environment is designed without writing code, facilitating short iterations. Trace: [Article_13 §chunk::33]

and.name: Multi_Paradigm_Modelling
and.description: An approach to explicitly model system aspects using the most appropriate formalisms and abstraction levels, while explicitly modeling the development process. Trace: [Article_4 §chunk::5; Article_4 §chunk::6]

and.name: System_Specification_Goals

and.name: Shared_Attributes_Specification

and.name: Linking_Multiple_Facets
and.description: The objective of linking the multiple facets of a system under design. Trace: [Article_1 §Introduction]

and.name: Process_Stakeholder_Intentions
and.description: The goals and intentions of process stakeholders that define the role of each model in the federation. Trace: [Article_13 §chunk::25]

and.name: Correct_by_Construction
and.description: An objective to produce a correct implementation by ensuring global consistency across all viewpoints. Trace: [Article_13 §chunk::4]

and.name: Architectural_Understanding

and.name: Reuse_Enhancement
and.description: The objective of formalizing component interrelationships to achieve increased reuse of MDE components. Trace: [Article_14 §chunk::3]

and.name: Integration_specific_Views
and.description: The goal of providing dedicated languages and models that serve as views specifically for integration purposes. Trace: [Article_3 §chunk::148]

and.name: Documentation
and.description: An application of the FTG+PM model to summarize the different languages used, required operations, and the process flow. Trace: [Article_4 §chunk::16]

and.name: Design_Decisions
and.description: The set of decisions made based on specific requirements and realized through implementation artifacts. Trace: [Article_5 §chunk::7]

and.name: Centralized_Understanding
and.description: The goal of maintaining a centralized understanding of the overall information model within a distributed architecture. Trace: [Article_6 §chunk::13]

and.name: VV_A
and.description: Support for verification, validation, and accreditation processes to ensure system correctness and compliance. Trace: [Article_7 §chunk::21]

and.name: Reduced_Maintenance
and.description: A benefit of MDE where high-level models allow reasoning about requirements independently of implementation, easing maintenance. Trace: [Article_7 §chunk::0]

and.name: Shorter_Development_Time
and.description: A benefit of MDE achieved by focusing on high-level models and decoupling architectural decisions. Trace: [Article_7 §chunk::0]

and.name: Modularity
and.description: The degree to which a system's components may be separated and recombined, covering structural and conceptual aspects. Trace: [Article_8 §chunk::4; Article_8 §chunk::42]

and.name: Structural_Modularity
and.description: Modularity related to the structure and organization of system components. Trace: [Article_8 §chunk::42]

and.name: Conceptual_Modularity
and.description: Modularity related to the conceptual separation and organization of system concerns. Trace: [Article_8 §chunk::42]

and.name: Abstraction
and.description: The process of removing physical, spatial, or temporal details to focus on essential aspects in modeling. Trace: [Article_8 §chunk::4]

and.name: Global_Consistency
and.description: The state of consistency across all models in the system, achieved through synchronization. Trace: [Article_8 §chunk::15]

and.name: Cross_Model_Traceability
and.description: The ability to trace relationships and dependencies across different heterogeneous models to support feedback and co-evolution. Trace: [Article_9 §chunk::4]

and.name: Interoperability_Goals

and.name: Interoperability

and.name: Reusability

and.name: Composability

and.name: High_Cohesion

and.name: Tool_and_Platform_Neutral_Usage

and.name: Seamless_Integration
and.description: The integration of specialized formalisms and tools in a way that appears smooth and continuous to the user. Trace: [Article_8 §chunk::15]

and.name: Security_Goals

and.name: Confidentiality
and.description: A security property ensuring that information is not disclosed to unauthorized entities. Trace: [Article_11 §chunk::14]

and.name: Accountability

and.name: Privacy

and.name: Integrity

and.name: Authentication

and.name: Authorization

and.name: Quality_Assessment

and.name: Question_Level
and.description: The middle level of the GQM measurement system used to define the set of viewpoints that constitute the multimodel. Trace: [Article_12 §chunk::16]

and.name: Metric_Level
and.description: The bottom level of the GQM measurement system providing specific metrics for evaluation. Trace: [Article_12 §chunk::16]

and.name: Continuous_Maturity_Improvement

and.name: Efficiency

and.name: Usability
